newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 8.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Chinese Ambassador has shown that the race debate in Australia is effecting relations with China, as even after a strong bipartisan motion was passed last week by Federal Parliament, Ambassador Hua Junduo, went and raised the issue with senior Australian officials in Canberra on Monday. Page 1.

The Federal Government said yesterday faster economic growth was necessary to slow the current rising of the jobless number in Australia, following the release of Australian Bureau of Statistics unemployment figures for October which showed unemployment a 8.8 per cent in seasonally adjusted terms, up slightly from September. Page 3.

The ACTU is building up funds to assist unions fight major industrial disputes and defend legal actions brought by employers. The fund is seen as defending basic union principles such as the right to strike and the right to bargain collectively. Page 4.

The Chief Justice of the Industrial Relations Court, Murray Wilcox, yesterday ruled that female flight attendants who were forced to retire at age 35 during the 1980s because of sex discrimination by Qantas Airways, were entitled to reinstatement last year with full seniority. Murray admitted the decision disadvantaged 823 flight attendants with continuous service. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Martin Bryant, on trial in Hobart for the world's worst massacre by a lone gunman at Port Arthur on April 28, yesterday pleaded guilty to the murder of 35 people. Reversing his original plea of not guilty, Bryant also pleaded guilty to 20 charges of attemted murder, as well as charges of wounding, aggravated assault, causing grievous bodily harm, arson and unlawfully setting fire to a building. As Bryant pleaded to the charges, he laughed out loud to the packed courtroom. Page 1.

The Federal Government yesterday talked up the outlook for growth and accused the Opposition's pessimism of damaging the economy, despite the release of figures revealing a further rise in unemployment and confirming slow growth. Seasonally adjusted unempoyment rose in October from 8.7 to 8.8 per cent. Page 1.

The Federal Government yesterday accused the Opposition of undermining confidence in the immigration program as the Senate rejected key elements of the Howard Government's proposal to cut the immigration intake from 83,000 in 1995-96 to 74,000 this financal year. Immigration Minister Phillip Ruddock warned that
he would now have to resort to draconian measures under the Migration Act to limit numbers. Page 3.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has all but ruled out using the Federal Government's media ownership review as a platform to liberalise foreign ownership limits for newspapers and television. The Treasurer's comments have implied that Canadian media propietor Conrad Black, who has strongly urged for an increase in ownership levels, would be prevented from adding to his 25 per cent stake in John Fairfax Holdings. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After intensive talks with his counsel, Martin Bryant has reversed his original plea to "guilty" of the Port Arthur shootings. In a packed courtroom filled with emotion, Bryant laughed as he answered "guilty" to the charges of killing 35 people in April erlier this year. Page 1.

The Senate yesterday rejected a range of measures proposed by the Federal Government which would have produced fewer immigrants by making it more difficult for applicants to gain entry to Australia. Immigration Minister Phillip Ruddock warned the Senate's behaviour would sabotage public confidence in the immigration program. Page 1.

A note left by former judge David Yeldham before he took his own life on Monday should not be made public, according to a statement issued by his family, because the note contained matters which might be relevant to paedophilia matters being investigated by the New South Wales Police Royal Commission. Page 1.

After Australia's jobless number passed the 800,000 mark for the first time in two years Prime Minister John Howard yesterday declared unemployment a challenge demanding "even faster" rates of economic growth, confirming earlier fears that growth of around three per cent was not enough to halt the growing numbers of unemployed. Page 2.
THE AGE

The survivors of the Port Arthur massacre have been spared a lengthy court case after Martin Bryant reversed his pleas yesterday, admitting guilt to all the charges arising from the shootings. Witnesses and relatives of the victims expressed relief last nght, for the reversal of the plea has ensured a brief trial and early sentencing. Page A1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday said he would stand by his pledge to create 150,000 jobs in Victoria by the turn of the century after his State's unemployment figures rose to 9.5 per cent. The 0.1 per cent rise this month is the fifth monthly
incease in a row for Victoria. Page A1.

17-year-old Kristy McDonald was forced to wait for three hours in the back seat of a car, suffering from liver transplant complications because the Austin Medical Centre's emergency department was full, her parents said yesterday. Page A1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday attracted the ire of the Law Institute of Victoria and the Victims of Crimes Assistance League after he suggested on radio 3AW that solicitors took a large share of payments awarded to victims in the Crimes Compenstion Tribunal and he had decided to change the system for compensating crime victims because people had not been spending money on trying to heal their illness. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
